category: Planninq competes as team project and task management inside Nextcloud: projects with members, a kanban board per project with work in progress limits, a backlog, a task page with comments, attachments and dependencies, a per-project Gantt timeline, due reminders, personal time logging with a timesheet, and a capacity and portfolio view across projects, for internal IT, development and project teams in Dutch public organisations. It is project planning and work management. It is not rostering or shift planning (humaniq owns that) and not booking of rooms or equipment. A buyer who already runs Nextcloud compares it first with Nextcloud Deck, which is on the same platform for free, then with the open source project management suites OpenProject, Plane and Kanboard, and with the market leader Jira, which the product's own description names as the complexity it avoids.

The missing half is planninq's: src/views/TaskDetail.vue has no @mention listener, so the owner moved to ConductionNL/planninq (nextcloud-vue lane) (nextcloud-vue lane, OpenSpec pass 2026-09-27; owner was ConductionNL/nextcloud-vue). Owner moved to ConductionNL/planninq under learniq corpus decision D10 (planninq owns the timetable, learniq reads sessions from it); state untouched (learniq lane, OpenSpec pass 2026-09-27; owner was ConductionNL/learniq). Owner-moves pass 2026-09-28: decided-no. Setting up an A and B week cycle and period versions is timetable construction in the rostering system. The fleet does not build timetables: learniq openspec/changes/archive/2026-07-16-timetabling-and-substitution/design.md:25 ('does not generate a timetable') and the Non-Goals entry at :59 ('Timetable generation / constraint-solving optimisation (Zermelo's/Untis's job, permanently)'), adopted for planninq by decision D10: planninq receives a generated timetable from the rostering system through integriq and stores dated sessions (school-timetable-target, planninq PR #685).
